subject: Executive compact: scope consolidation and sensitive HR handoff
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>, Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@talentpartners.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Executive compact: scope consolidation and sensitive HR handoff

Team —

Following our leadership sync yesterday, I put together a compact proposal to consolidate overlapping scope between the Serving Runtime optimization squad and the Latency Tools pod into a single small leadership umbrella. The goal is to reduce duplicated ownership on kernel selection and runtime telemetry, while keeping the day-to-day engineering capacity intact.

High level:
- Merge "Serving Runtime - Optimization" (4 ICs, 1 senior IC lead) and "Latency Tools" (3 ICs, 1 senior IC lead) into a single "Inference Runtime & Tools" group reporting to Marcus.
- Create a new senior engineering manager role (1.0 FTE) for operational alignment; promote one of the existing senior ICs to that manager with a revised scope.
- Re-scope remaining IC roles to clearer domain boundaries (kernel selection, telemetry/observability, batching). See attached role-scopes.xlsx and an org-chart-draft.pdf for the suggested mapping.

Sensitive HR notes (important):
- One individual on the Serving Runtime side has been performance-flagged in the June review and will require a private 1:1 and calibrated expectations before any public announcement. We want HR in the loop before any broad comms.
- Timing constraints: product is shipping an internal benchmark next month; we should avoid any broad changes that could add confusion during the ship window.

Asks:
1) Marcus & Lauren — please confirm feasibility from an execution and resourcing perspective. Any objections to the proposed reporting line to Marcus?
2) Jonas & Mina — can you review the role descriptions in role-scopes.xlsx for clarity and risks, particularly around career laddering and leveling implications?
3) Claire — would appreciate HR’s recommended sequence for private 1:1s, manager talking points, and any legal/notice considerations. See confidential_handling_guidelines.pdf attached.

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Sep 3–7: Manager-level alignment and private 1:1s with affected ICs (HR present for the flagged person)
- Sep 10: Leadership sign-off
- Sep 13: Broad comms to the group (short post + Q&A)

I want to be explicit: this is not a public announcement yet. Please reply with availability and any redlines by EOD Sep 2 so we can decide whether to proceed this cycle or defer until after the product milestone.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
VP, Platform Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: org-chart-draft.pdf (diagram), role-scopes.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference>, Claire Dawson <claire.dawson@talentpartners.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive compact: scope consolidation and sensitive HR handoff

Ava — thanks for laying this out. High-level thoughts:

1) Reporting to me is fine from a line-management standpoint; operationally I want to preserve a clear tech lead path so we don't unintentionally create competing manager/IC dynamics.

2) Timing concern: the internal benchmark release is scheduled for Sep 9. Moving all private 1:1s into Sep 3–7 is tight for managers who are also heads-down on validation runs. Can we extend private 1:1s through Sep 10 with a hard leadership decision on Sep 13? That gives teams breathing room and avoids last-minute churn during benchmark runs.

3) Compensation/leveling: if we're promoting a senior IC to EM, we need to sync with People Ops on leveling and comp adjustments before any announcement. I recommend a calibrated check with compensation (Mina) before leadership sign-off.

4) For the flagged person: let's make sure the manager has a clear script and list of examples (not just impressions). Claire — can your templates include a short "observations + expectations" script we can use?

I'll review the attachments this afternoon and leave inline comments.

— Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime

All — quick read, and I appreciate keeping HR looped early. A couple of practical items to consider:

- Split reporting: rather than a single EM role taking all reports, consider a dotted-line model for telemetry/observability to Product so roadmap prioritization remains neutral. That reduces perceived favoritism when we reassign tickets and prioritization.

- Performance review window: our Q3 calibration closes Sep 14. If we make any role changes before calibration completes, we risk inconsistent ladder outcomes for people currently mid-cycle. For the flagged individual I suggest HR coordinates a private calibration note with their reviewer so it's captured appropriately.

- Communication tone: keep the first manager 1:1 conservative — acknowledge contributions, explain the business rationale, and outline next-step support (training / re-scope / probation window).

I'll add comments on role-scopes.xlsx (career-level mapping).

— Lauren
Head of Product Operations

Thanks for including me, Ava. A few quick, practical suggestions from People Ops/legal perspective: 

1) For the flagged individual, do not conflate restructuring with performance management. We should have a separate, documented private conversation outlining observed performance gaps and the support plan. If a PIP is likely, follow the PIP checklist and have it reviewed with legal.

2) Templates: I attached confidential_handling_guidelines.pdf with an "observations + examples" script and a manager checklist for a sensitive 1:1. Use the manager checklist in the private meeting and store notes in the confidential HR folder.

3) Timeline: I recommend the Sep 3–14 private 1:1 window you proposed but allow managers to extend by up to 48 hours if they need to finish critical deployment work. Avoid broad comms until Sep 15 at the earliest.

4) Compensation/leveling: Mina should coordinate with comp to draft the proposed promotion package. If promotion involves leveling change, run it through the formal comp committee next Tuesday (Sep 8).

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow to walk managers through the script.

— Claire Dawson
Senior HR Partner, TalentPartners (external)

Attachment: confidential_handling_guidelines.pdf
